walkthroughs.body_html:
The Church of England is the established church — bishops sit in the House of Lords and the monarch is its Supreme Governor.

Around a third of state-funded schools in England are faith schools (mostly CofE and Catholic).

Critics call this unfair in a multi-faith society; supporters say it offers high quality moral education and parental choice.

UK law generally protects the right to wear religious dress — turbans, hijabs, crosses — under the Human Rights Act 1998.

The UK abolished the blasphemy law in 2008. Free speech includes the right to criticise religion, but incitement to religious hatred is illegal (Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006).

Both Christianity and Islam condemn extremism. Pope Francis and Muslim leaders signed the Document on Human Fraternity in Abu Dhabi (2019), calling religious violence a betrayal of God.

Interfaith dialogue (e.g. the Council of Christians and Jews, founded 1942) builds tolerance and understanding — a strong evaluation point against extremism.
